$comment: AUTHORED declaration of which ccusage child calls each usage.py subcommand makes, and in
what order. Read out of usage.py by hand at commit b54501f; every entry cites its line.
This is deliberately NOT generated by instrumenting a run. Instrumentation only ever finds
the argv that the run it watched happened to produce, so a subcommand that stopped calling
ccusage — or quietly started calling it twice — would simply redefine the 'expected' set and
agree with itself forever. The direction of trust runs the other way here: this file states
what should happen, the recorder observes what did, and build.py --check compares them.
Shape names below refer to the five argv forms in `shapes`. There are exactly five call
sites in usage.py and each one builds exactly one of these.
$anchorComment: The wall clock every unanchored case is recorded at.
45 of the 118 cases carry their own `captureAnchor` (they have stored goldens); the other
73 are differential-only and carry none, because tests-ts/parity.mjs runs them at a LIVE
anchor — it is asking whether the two implementations agree today, not replaying a fixed
A live anchor cannot be used here. `--since -3d` resolves against the anchor, so the child
argv (and therefore the artifact key) would change every day, and a COMMITTED artifact set
keyed on it would rot overnight. So unanchored cases are recorded at this fixed date, and
the artifact set is explicitly anchor-relative.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REPLAYER (ISS-019): a replay driven at a live anchor will look up keys
this index does not contain. That is a real constraint, not an oversight — the replayer
must either pin its anchors to the recorded ones or treat relative-date cases as requiring
the live oracle. It is written down here so that whoever builds the replayer meets it as a
stated design fact rather than as a mysterious lookup miss.

daily.why: cmd_daily builds the daily argv directly. usage.py:497.

why: cmd_share calls agg_projects(a.since, a.until) at usage.py:517, and AGAIN as
agg_projects(a.vs, None) at usage.py:520 only when --vs is given. Note the second
call passes until=None regardless of --until: the comparison window is open-ended.
ONE call, not two. cmd_compare issues instances(min(d1,d2), max(d1,d2)) at
usage.py:555 — a single request spanning both days, then splits the rows locally.
Reading 'two calendar days, side by side' as two child calls is the obvious wrong
guess and is why this is written down.

blocks.why: cmd_blocks builds the blocks argv directly. usage.py:578.

why: cmd_hourly -> instances(date, date) at usage.py:604, with the SAME compact date on
both ends (a single calendar day).
This entry was first authored as `calls: []` on the reasoning that hourly 'reads raw
logs directly' — which it does, at usage.py:619, but only for the histogram BUCKETS.
It still asks ccusage for the per-family effective $/token RATE that turns those
bucketed tokens into dollars, and it makes that call unconditionally, before the glob.
The recorder observed the call, build.py --check reported the contradiction, and
usage.py:604 settled it against the declaration. Left written down because 'hourly is
the log-reading command' is the intuition that produced the wrong entry, and it is
persuasive enough to produce it again.

alltime.why: cmd_alltime -> agg_projects(None, None) at usage.py:658 — unwindowed.

why: cmd_codex -> agg_codex, which calls codex_sessions(since_key, None) and then
codex_daily(since_key, until_key) at usage.py:360.
TWO details that are easy to get wrong:
* codex_sessions is ALWAYS passed until=None, deliberately (usage.py:334-336):
last-activity >= since is a safe superset of started-in-window, and a real
--until would wrongly drop sessions that started in-window but ran past it.
The windowing is then done locally off the rollout filename's start date.
* codex_daily is called UNCONDITIONALLY, even though its result is only DISPLAYED
for windowed runs (the delta cross-check). An unwindowed codex case still makes
this call.
cmd_combined -> agg_projects(since, until) at usage.py:676, then agg_codex(since,
until) at usage.py:677, which contributes the same two codex calls as above.

$unexercisedComment: Window args that usage.py demonstrably passes but that NO case in the registry ever
supplies. Each is a hole in the parity suite, filed as ISS-029.
They are listed by name rather than quietly tolerated because build.py --check otherwise
reads windowArgs permissively: it says which extra args are ALLOWED, so an arg declared
here and never observed is contradicted by nothing, and widening a shape would be
undetectable. (Measured — adding --until to `blocks` was the one mutation the checker
originally missed.) Requiring every declared arg to be observed UNLESS it appears below
makes the loophole exactly as wide as this list. build.py also fails on a STALE entry, so
adding the missing cases forces the entry's removal rather than leaving it to rot.

why: usage.py:580 appends --since, but all 10 blocks cases are bare `blocks` or `blocks -h`.
blocks has NO windowed case at all, and --since is its only window arg, so nothing in
the parity suite touches that branch.
usage.py:501 appends --until. Three daily cases pass --since; none passes --until.
usage.py:266 appends --until and cmd_codex does reach it (usage.py:360), but all 8
codex/combined cases are unwindowed or --since-only. Worse here than elsewhere: with
no --until case, a port that wrongly forwarded --until to codex_sessions as well would
look identical in the trace to one that correctly withholds it (usage.py:334-336).

$helpComment: argparse handles these at PARSE time: it prints usage and calls sys.exit(0) before the
subcommand's func ever runs, so any argv containing one makes no child call no matter what
command it names. `projects --since 20260101 -h` is a real registry case and exits 0 having
called nothing. This is declared here rather than special-cased silently in build.py so
that the exemption is visible next to the commands it overrides.
notes: Cases that never reach a child call at all — argv errors, --help, and the deliberately
broken CCUSAGE_CMD in err_missing_binary — declare no command here and are expected to
produce an empty trace. build.py --check treats 'declared nothing, observed something' as
a failure in the same way as the reverse.
